content: Escherichia coli O104:H21 is a rare serotype of the bacterial species Escherichia coli, which normally resides in the lower intestines of mammals. While many serotypes of E. coli are either beneficial or non-pathogenic, E. coli O104:H21 is recognized as a pathogenic strain. This specific serotype was first identified in 1982 during an outbreak of severe bloody diarrhea. The outbreak was traced to undercooked hamburgers that had been contaminated with the bacteria. E. coli O104:H21 is capable of causing outbreaks of infection similar to those caused by E. coli O157:H7, which is the most common shiga-like toxin-producing E. coli (SLTEC). SLTECs are well-known for being significant causes of gastrointestinal illnesses and diarrhea. In most cases, the human body is able to eliminate harmful E. coli O104:H21 on its own within 5 to 10 days. The use of antibiotics is not recommended, as they may worsen the condition. Similarly, antidiarrheal agents such as loperamide should be avoided.
